A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RePro study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures, prompts, and examples, are readable and support reliable comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original 400M and 1.4B pretraining results, reward ablations, efficiency measurements, and analyses of recycled data.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds another rephraser, 2.8B pretraining experiments, controlled comparisons, additional ablations, and baseline variance estimates.

M1.justification: The GRPO procedure, four reward functions, filtering and mixing pipeline, and default rephrasing prompt remain unchanged. OLMo2-1B is added as a base-model configuration using the same method; no new algorithmic component or architectural modification is described.

E1.justification: Both versions use DCLM-RefinedWeb and the same 22 downstream tasks, listed in v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 12. The FLAN reference for the influence-reward experiment is also retained. Larger pools and quality-based subsets remain within existing coverage; FineWeb and RedPajama are proposed only for future validation.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds reward-aware Prompting+ and SFT+ comparators and Nemotron-CC Diverse QA using Qwen3-30B-A3B. Figure 3 also adds WRAP and ProX to the existing token-budget comparison, which previously compared RePro only with organic data. These substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: v2 adds OLMo2-1B initialization and 2.8B pretraining with a 144B-token pool and 55.9B/84.7B training budgets. New protocols include a 115.2B-token compute-equalized organic baseline, matched-source and matched-rephraser ReWire comparisons, source-quality fractions, and sampling-parameter sweeps. The original smaller-model main settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test excluding high-quality sources from recycling, the origins of selected recycled examples, recycled-only versus mixed training, and sensitivity to temperature and top-p. Appendix D adds quality-stratified examples and prompting cases. Earlier reward dynamics, reward-weight studies, and quality-selection analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v1 provides no pretraining seed-variability estimates. v2 Appendix B.4 and Table 8 report three organic-pool sampling seeds, per-category and Core standard deviations, and comparisons against twice those deviations. This is limited to the 400M organic baseline; v2 explicitly states that the full recycling pipeline was not replicated across seeds.

E6.justification: The original Qwen3-4B main results remain, including Core scores of 0.21658 and 0.29929. v2 adds substantial results for new configurations and controls: at 2.8B/55.9B training tokens, OLMo2-based RePro scores 0.36691 versus 0.35390 for organic data. Figure 4 newly reports 63.5% low-quality-source recovery, versus 31.0%-42.5% for comparators.

T1.justification: v2 Equations 11-12 introduce explicit definitions partitioning high-quality recycled examples by whether their organic sources were low- or high-quality. The existing recycling, reward, and GRPO mathematics is retained; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The headline contribution expands from a 4B rephraser outperforming ReWire to a 1B rephraser, 70 times smaller than ReWire's generator, doubling its performance gains. Claims now encompass 2.8B pretraining models, with the reported improvement range changing from 4.7%-14.0% to 3.7%-14.5%. The 2-3 times organic-data-efficiency claim is retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations concerning low-quality-data recovery, recycled data complementing organic data, OLMo2 adaptability, and faithful recycling versus knowledge distillation through QA generation. Appendix A adds task-category interpretations. New qualifications acknowledge baseline-only variance estimation, untested transfer to other corpora, and residual generator bias.

D1.justification: v2 adds 2.8B training hyperparameters, the enhanced comparator prompt, OLMo2 compute costs, and threshold-selection rationale. It omits v1's explicit long-document splitting and concatenation instructions. The abstract's resource statement narrows from code, rephraser, and recycled data to code; the PDFs do not establish actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the OLMo2 report, The Synthetic Data Playbook, Rubrics as Rewards, and FineWeb, while removing Zhu and Hauff's BERT-based reward citation. These support localized additions about rephraser size, reward design, and future coverage; the central related-work positioning remains.

P1.justification: The evaluation narrative is substantially reorganized: training dynamics and distributional analyses are combined, operation analysis joins the source-quality discussion, and alternative reward analysis moves to the appendix. The appendices gain a contents guide, category discussion, regrouped experimental details, and subdivided case studies. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are revised accordingly.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference layout. Main tables expand, five additional numbered tables appear, and Figure 3 changes from a two-series horizontal chart to a five-series grouped vertical chart. A new four-panel source-quality figure and additional comparison boxes are added; retained figures are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence through compute-equalized organic comparisons and matched-source/model ReWire controls, addressing important attribution gaps in v1. Stronger comparators, another rephraser family, and larger and longer pretraining runs further test the central conclusions. Uncertainty remains restricted to the 400M organic baseline despite broader main-text wording, and omitted long-document instructions modestly weaken reproducibility. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support.
